dlg.1: Hi, coach. How can I help?
dlg.7:
Hey there!

Nilo here, your guide through the Great Clock, the world you just tumbled into. So, what are you curious about?
dlg.8: Sounds good. What's on your mind?
dlg.10: Right, to the training arena with you. A Lanudo is waiting there, and it adores a good punch-up. Don't hold back.
dlg.11: Your spot in the rankings and your card collection are your two main goals! To climb the rankings of the Great Clock, string wins together in the arena against other players and prove you're the strongest. Winning fights also earns you cards for your grimoire. You can also get them from the Card Masters and the fusion altars (Services). For now, start with the Story and rack up some wins.
dlg.12: Three brawling routes exist in the Great Clock. Story is your solo adventure: your fighters level up battle by battle, but they wear down, get bruised and, if things go wrong, they're gone for good. Ranked hands everyone the same stats and expects you to know your stuff, so save it for later. If nobody's online, you can take on a player's ghost instead. Tournaments run on their own house rules and pay out tokens and cards you won't find anywhere else.
dlg.14: Tell me how the folks you fight are real people too.
dlg.15: Your pass to Demon I's den. Once you're inside he'll explain some combat ideas worth your time.
dlg.17: Tell me how the folks you fight are real people too.
dlg.18: Here, a card that unlocks the hideout of Demon I. There he can pass on a handful of combat know-how.
dlg.20: Tell me how the folks you fight are real people too.
dlg.22: I've got something to tell you.
dlg.23: Hi, I have a message for you.
dlg.24: Here's the answer you were after.
dlg.30: I've got something to tell you.
dlg.34: Tell me how the folks you fight are real people too.
dlg.35: I've got something to tell you.
dlg.42: None: the Great Clock is a world of its own, with its own rules. Everything here is won by playing: fights, tournaments, trades and fusion altars. Nothing is bought with real money.
dlg.44: Once you have beaten Demon III's challenges (Story), go and see Demon I: he will teach you useful tactics for your next fights.
dlg.45:
Hey!

Back in my day I was the Elite mode champ. Ask away.
dlg.46:
Elite mode is for coaches who have already mastered every spell and equipable item in the game. In Elite mode you get a budget of 6000 points to build your team and give your fighters spells and gear. Even if you're new to Elite, you start with as many points as the best Elite players and get the same spells and gear as them. Everyone fights on the same level.

Your Elite level goes up when you win and down when you lose. Thanks to it, the demons will try to find you an opponent your own size.
dlg.47:
In your team management window, click the «Elite» tab. You'll see three ready-made teams to practise with and learn how teams are built.

Create a new team when you feel ready. Then add fighters by clicking «Recruit».

Remember, you only have 6000 budget points, not one more. So you'll need to pick 2 or 3 well-equipped fighters with plenty of spells, or 5 or 6 less-equipped ones who win by numbers.
dlg.48:
Perfect, I've got two challenges that suit you well.

In the first, you'll need to watch exactly where you stand in the arena and use your Healer's cures at just the right moment.

In the second, you'll have to coordinate your team members and their abilities to beat your enemies.
dlg.49: The longer your winning streak runs, the better your odds of pulling a card from each win. Just remember: the higher your level, the scarcer and shinier those cards get.
dlg.50:
Ow! Stupid dagger... and I'm still dripping! How is a ghost even supposed to bleed?

Oh, a newcomer. Come closer, I'll walk you through Evolution mode. Ask away.
dlg.51: Evolution mode is the best choice if you've just arrived in the Great Clock. Thanks to the sphere tree, you'll gradually unlock spells and equipment for each of your fighters, so they're easier to learn and building your first team gets simpler. In this mode your fighters get stronger and stronger: as you chain fights, a fighter's power is set by its rank. The league you play in depends on the rank of your strongest fighter. The higher the league, the more cards and reputation you earn. Reputation is what levels you up, and it decides your ranking for the current season. Watch out, though: fighters can get injured, for example if they fight while too tired. To avoid that and earn more experience or reputation, use the bonuses from consumables and equipment sets. Finally, remember that in Evolution mode you don't lose levels. Don't be scared of defeat: it even earns you reputation and experience! Just don't overwork your fighters: rotate your substitutes to limit your team's fatigue.
dlg.52: In Evolution you only have one team and a bench of substitutes. Create your fighters straight into this team using the recruit buttons. To change your team, send the fighters you want to the bench and recruit new ones in their place, or bring back the ones already on the bench. BUT WATCH OUT! You can only remove 4 fighters per week. I'd recommend studying each class and its skills in your overview (a tab in your inventory).
dlg.53: The sphere tree shows a fighter's learning. It's made of spheres you buy with the experience gained in combat. You can only buy the sphere directly next on the path to the one where the progress cursor sits (shown as your fighter's head). Once bought, spheres give bonuses: a stat boost, a new spell, or a set of equipment unlocked for that fighter. Watch out, some spheres also carry penalties: a sacrifice the fighter must make to keep progressing. There are special spheres too, like portal spheres that teleport you to another point on the tree, or barrier spheres that ask you to sacrifice a card to open the way. Learning to move through the tree wisely makes your fighters more effective, and faster. It's a game in itself!
dlg.54: If you've been listening to what we've told you about Evolution mode, you know your fighters can get injured and need healing. An unhealed fighter takes penalties in combat and is very likely to see the wound get worse. There's only one way to heal a wound: use a healing card, which you can get through a trade or in packs you buy with tokens on the game's website. It's magic: with that, everything grows back! Well... almost everything!
dlg.55:
Winning cards works differently in Evolution mode. Here you get bonuses to improve your chance of finding cards (collection) and of finding rare ones (prospecting).

These bonuses come mostly from the equipment sets you wear. On top of that, the higher your level and the higher the leagues you fight in, the more cards you'll get when you win.

In Evolution mode it's usually easier to get cards than in the other modes, which makes sense: you also have to spend them, for example on healing.
dlg.56: Hey, you! Hold that thought. Not my reflection, my twin. The Brumas pair ruled 2vs2 back in the day. So, what's on your mind?
dlg.57: 2vs2 mode lets you create an Elite team with a friend and share control of the fighters, so you can steer them together in the arena. It's a lot of fun, because you and your teammate need to know each other very well and communicate fast if you want to win.
dlg.58:
In your team management window, click the 2vs2 tab.
Create a new team with one of the creation buttons at the bottom of the window. To confirm it, pick a friend from your friend list to share it with and give the team a name. Then add fighters by clicking «Recruit».
Remember, you only have 6000 budget points, not one more: you'll need to choose between 2 or 3 well-equipped fighters with plenty of spells, or 5 or 6 less-equipped ones who rely on numbers. Finally, before playing, just use the fighter sharing button to split them between you... and you're set!
dlg.59: Got some Gold-digger in you, have you? The more wins in a row you rack up, the better your chances of getting a card after a won fight. Of course, the higher your level, the rarer and more precious the cards will be.
dlg.60:
Hey, hello!

Come meet this old Gold-digger ghost, who gave the tournament crowd a real headache back in the day. What can I tell you?
dlg.61:
Tournament mode is a separate mode. I'll tell you a bit about it, but don't jump in until you've mastered at least one of the other modes!

In the Great Clock, at least one tournament is held every day, usually at set times. You can see all the upcoming tournaments with the calendar icon at the bottom of your interface.

What makes tournaments special is that the rules change from one to the next: the budget may change, some spells may be banned, and plenty of other things too.

To take part, you have to sign up, then create a team that can compete. When the time comes, you can select the tournament and your team from your own interface and search for an opponent.

You can even create your own tournament if you have the special «Tournament Creation» card.
dlg.62:
To register for a tournament, go to the tournament totem in the lobby, or use your calendar with its icon at the bottom of the interface.

Registration periods vary: sometimes you have to sign up before a certain date.

For other tournaments you need to hand over a card to register. These usually offer much better rewards.

Finally, some tournaments aren't open to everyone: they can be private and reserved for a guild or for the best players. Always read a tournament's description to learn its registration terms.
dlg.63: I like your spirit! By taking part in tournaments, you'll win tournament tokens. At the tournament hall, you can swap those tokens for exclusive cards. Some of those cards let you send items to other games, such as Vidalia. For example, you can send characteristic or spell scrolls, or even the famous Champion set!
dlg.65:
So you've wandered into my lair.

Demon I, at your service. Want advanced combat know-how? Then go find my henchmen, the minute demons.
dlg.66: Easy: in the lobby, pick your next fight. Training puts you against the AI, Story carries on your campaign against the demons, Fight finds you a rival of your level in the Ranked ladder, and tournaments are in the Calendar. Before that, get your fighters ready in Team.
dlg.69: Yes! Just don't forget to face your fighters properly after every step and strike, or you'll be stuck at a disadvantage. You can also exploit how your rivals are lined up. Hitting from behind does 40% more damage. Hitting from the flank gives 20% more, so get sneaky. Those area and neutral hits miss out on the bonus, sadly.
dlg.71: I've got something to tell you.
dlg.73: I've got something to tell you.
dlg.74:
That's quite a lot to cover.
Which part exactly?
dlg.75: Cards come in four shades, depending on how scarce they are: - Black, the everyday ones. - Copper, the common crowd. - Silver, the ones that are hard to find. - Gold, the true jackpots.
dlg.76: This is where you face off against other players, real ones! Don't be shocked if you drop a few early matches while you find your rhythm. And the first win will feel amazing!
dlg.77: Your cards log all your belongings. That covers your gear, your fighters' moves, your coins, and whatever else you collect.
dlg.78: Spot on! Each card carries a price tag and gets used like cash. So the more you hoard, the richer you get. Swiping cards for everything is so handy nowadays, right?
dlg.79: Nope, not every one! Some cards double as pieces of armour, which you can simply put on. A card is really just a tag that keeps your inventory tidy. You don't put the card on, obviously! But mind the level: wear a piece that asks for level 15 while you're level 10 and you miss out on its bonuses. Wearing it anyway is still an option.
dlg.80: There are lots of ways to get cards. - When you win a fight you may take cards from the loot; after 10 loots without a rare one, the next brings one. - Every few wins in Ranked or against ghosts you pick 1 card out of 3. - You can trade with other players. - Some challenges give cards. - The Card Masters sell them. - Fusion altars make new cards. - And tournaments give exclusive cards.
dlg.81: Card Masters are, in a way, card sellers. You'll spot them scattered across the Great Clock. Every one stocks cards of different strength, and some are mobbed by coaches for that very reason. As I mentioned, buying means handing over other cards as payment: their combined value must cover the one you're after.
dlg.82: I'll explain it all in detail! A fusion altar lets you get a card by sacrificing other cards, following a recipe that's set in advance and often unknown! So you'll have to experiment to find the right recipes. Each fusion altar is different, and more or less powerful. A very powerful altar at full boost can even reach a 100% success rate! But a fusion's success rate depends on many factors, so here's how it works. There are fusion cards, made specifically to boost altars. So if you want to fuse very high-level cards, you need not only an extremely powerful altar but also a fusion card to boost your chances! What you need to remember: the more powerful the fusion you want, the harder it is to pull off. Put every chance on your side! That said, if a fusion fails, don't lose hope: depending on the altar's power, you may get some of the cards back. And remember, the most powerful cards can only be obtained this way. Who knows, you might come across a unique card nobody has ever seen.
dlg.83: Tackle is a move built into every fighter: when a rival slips past, you get a shot at pinning them in place, costing them their turn. It rolls on two stats, evasion and parry. Higher evasion means fewer chances of being pinned yourself. Higher parry means a better shot at pinning them. To check your odds of dodging the tackle on any tile, hover the cursor over the tile just ahead of the fighter preparing to move: a figure pops up.
dlg.84: Your grimoire is your Inventory: it shows which cards you have, what each one does and which collections you are missing. You also dress your coach from there, in Coach equipment. It's essential!

eventl.1: Among the Swordsmen, hitting hard is practically a religion. Today you pray with your blade, and the gods forgive the bruises.
eventl.10: Gamblers cry at the sight of a four-leaf clover just as happily as at a beaten rival. Today luck smiles on them, and maybe on you too.
eventl.11: The Bulwark goddess lends you a plated cuirass that takes a beating. Don't trust it blindly: it promises more than it can deliver.
eventl.12: Nobody's bored, but we're not staying here until sunrise either. Let's get moving, the clock is ticking!
eventl.13: Bad luck picks on everyone equally... They say every cloud has a silver lining, though yours seems to have stayed at home today.
eventl.14: Fighting wears you out, not to mention the bruises. Even the best fighters need a moment to stretch their legs before getting back into it.
eventl.15: Did you really think you'd keep bouncing around forever? Party's over, coach.
eventl.16: Suddenly water doesn't agree with you: sea, river, rain, even the kitchen sink. Keep your head dry, cheeky one.
eventl.17: There's a smell of scorching in the air. One little spark and you'll be toasted like bread. Mind the matches.
eventl.18: Feeling breathless? Not even the vultures could fly in this stillness. Take a deep breath, nothing's blowing here.
eventl.19: It smells of sweat and tears in here. Just a drop of blood and everything would be perfect. Don't worry, all is well in war.
eventl.2: They say whoever steals an egg ends up stealing a cow. Shades love repeating that with a grin, and you know what they're plotting.
eventl.20: I swear by Vadoril, the most glorious miracle-worker alive, with a heart of gold and biceps of steel. Now everybody's feeling chipper!
eventl.21: Dorvana the archer, famous for her aim, heard a voice on the wind: 'Blood's coming, and it'll splash everywhere!' Quite the omen, isn't it?
eventl.22: Nothing moves you? You strike first and never ask questions? Then feast your eyes: a slaughter fit only for the toughest.
eventl.23: Your wisdom is about to rhyme with your enemy's fear. Impossible? Just wait and see.
eventl.24: You can't see the air, but you'll feel this wind. It goes straight to your stomach and gives you courage.
eventl.25: Chant this ten times out loud: 'Wave spirit, make my foe quake and shrink their robes!' Easy magic, proven results.
eventl.26: This rock crumbles all by itself, and you never know when. Watch where you step: you've been warned.
eventl.27: The fight won't end? Panda's here with a round on the house while you keep slaughtering, without ever having to stop.
eventl.3: 'All together, charge the foe!' The war cry every Fury loves. Their goddess sheds one tear, and you shed whatever it takes to win.
eventl.4: 'A stitch in time saves nine, and a heal in time saves a life.' With sayings like that, Healers mend anything that moves, and even what doesn't.
eventl.43: Our last experiments drew a blank, so our specialist is busy brooding. Meanwhile the summons are run off their feet.
eventl.44: Trying to stop the flow of time, our 'expert' only managed to start a brawl among the summoned creatures.
eventl.45: Our tinkerer is patching up the Great Clock's faces. Heads up: his latest tinkering might come out a bit wonky.
eventl.46: Our field agent, Morvinel, swears the summons have picked up new tricks, chiefly the knack of soaking up more punishment.
eventl.47: We've lost contact with Morvinel. All we heard was a bear's roar, the kind only a Tamer can produce.
eventl.48: Gamblers are sentimental souls: a five-leaf clover moves them as much as a fallen foe.
eventl.49: Ruin and carnage are the scripture of the Swordsmen... and butchery is a sacrament too. Now go hit harder, champ.
eventl.5: It seems that when the Gardener made his Gardenettes, he gave them quite the temper. He also made docile dolls, in case you need one.
eventl.50: Her followers worship her for teaching them to nock arrows with flair and speed.
eventl.51: 'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.' With sayings like that, Healers mend anyone and anything that moves.
eventl.52: The Bulwark goddess offers you a true breastplate, plated armour. Tell me how it goes; it'll likely save you more than once.
eventl.53: 'Everyone at the Fury, and the Fury for everyone!' Every Fury shouts it before charging. Their goddess weeps tears of blood, and that blood gives you the nerve to endure any fight!
eventl.54: The Clockmaker is a discreet god, showing himself only to those who trust him. Deep, right? It might just open your mind.
eventl.55: 'Raise shades and they'll empty your pockets.' Old sayings are so often true, and they put Shades in such a good mood.
eventl.56: Still fighting? Everyone's off toasting a win or sulking over a loss. Panda offers the same, and keeps the axe handy.
eventl.57: Watching a Gold-digger run is a strange sight. Astonish your friends: the Gold-digger god has just gifted you great freedom of movement.
eventl.58: Tamers love their pets, and their god knows it! Stabbing an enemy with a Trufo, tearing them apart with a Mirgon... that's the good life!
eventl.59: When the Gardener made his Gardenettes, he gave them quite the temper. Luckily, he also makes docile dolls to order.
eventl.6: Tamers, who doesn't love animals? Your deity is well aware. Skewer foes with a Trufo, carve them up with a Mirgon... ain't life grand?
eventl.61: The time demon Ak'bal gives you a first push. You'll feel the energy, but don't get comfortable: the clock never forgives.
eventl.62: Ak'bal comes back with a second push. You've got the rhythm now, haven't you? Keep it up.
eventl.63: Ak'bal's third push stretches time in your favour. Make the most of it, the countdown waits for no one.
eventl.64: Ak'bal sends a first curse: time grows heavy and your strength slips away. Nothing you can't endure... almost.
eventl.65: Ak'bal's second curse. The minutes weigh more than they seem, so don't get distracted by the hands.
eventl.66: Ak'bal's third curse, the heaviest. The Great Clock has decided you'll take things slowly today. Breathe and carry on.
eventl.67: From Erabon's corner came a bear's roar that shook the walls. Nobody dared ask where it came from.
eventl.7: Think of the gold waiting at a rainbow's end. Our archer goddess is similar, minus the fairy tale: the bow is genuine and the bounty is redder...
eventl.8: Seeing a Gold-digger sprint leaves folks gaping. Show off to your mates! The Gold-digger god has gifted you plenty of room to move.
eventl.9: The Clockmaker never shows his face to doubters. Take our word for it, you'll see.

npc.91: What on earth is this? And where did you come from?
npc.92: Yuck! Can't even hop between dimensions these days without landing in a stinking garbage pit...
npc.93: Unless... this must be the Minute Demons' handiwork! They can't be far away, can they?
npc.94: I see, you have no idea what I'm talking about. Let me explain. My name is Altair. An Hour Demon has captured you, and you're being teleported to their world right now! Once you get there, you'll have to recruit a team of gladiators to fight for you...
npc.95: Pile up enough wins with your crew and you'll top the board and walk out free!
npc.96: Fail that and... oh well... it's game over for you!
npc.97: Hold on tight, this might rattle you a bit!
npc.98: I've got a few tips for you, and you'll regret skipping them.
npc.99: Take this one as a case in point...
npc.100: When I finally say 'hit the swords and a hunt for a rival begins', go ahead: tap them and the fight is on. Pretty slick, right? But hold off on it NOW...
npc.105: Next up is, no doubt, the most serious job of your coaching career: organizing your squad and gearing up your fighters.
npc.106: Press the glowing button to set up a fresh squad. Name it however you like, then hit OK.
npc.107: Next, hit 'Recruit'. Pick a class and a name, then tap 'Validate' to add the newcomer to your group.
npc.108: Dress your fighter in the Patchwork Hat, 100 pesetas a pop. Hunt it down in the list and double-tap it to put it on.
npc.109: Done! Now your fighter hits 15% harder with Earth. Don't know what Earth means? Then you haven't cracked open the manual, and that's a real shame!
npc.110: Feel free to close this window. Plenty is still waiting to be discovered, so I'll leave that fun to you.
npc.111: Click the swords and you'll hunt down a rival coach for a match. Before you do, put your squad through its paces and sharpen your tactics.
npc.113: Time to say goodbye. I'm shipping you off to meet your own kind. I'm out of here, this place reeks of demons...
npc.114: Also, go grab some spells for your crew. Slot them in like gear, just pick from the panel on the right. Trust me, they'll save your skin!
npc.117: Hmmm, you strike me as someone headed places.\n\nProve what you're made of in a fight. I could teach you a trick or two for staying alive... who knows? Someday you might fight for me in the arenas!
npc.118: You are in the lobby. Here you manage your coach. They can interact with other coaches (other players), objects and NPCs (non-player characters). Right-click to move, and left-click an object or player to interact with them. You can change and swap the clicks in the options menu.
npc.119: Battle in progress. Curious about the panels you see mid-fight? Chat with Demon III in the Great Clock, or check the matching chapter of the player's manual in the folder where you installed Pippop Arena.
npc.120: You've landed on the ranking screen. It lists the Pippop Arena players who shine brightest. Beside each name you'll see their strongest squad: power, wins and losses with that squad, and more.
npc.121: This is the coach statistics window.\n\nHere you'll find useful info about your account, like how long you've been playing Pippop Arena, or the total wins and losses of all your teams.
npc.122: Social screen: your friends, the people you've muted, and your clan all live here.\n
npc.123: You are in your coach's inventory window. It lists all the coach cards you own (the cards you win at the end of a fight, which are only used in the lobby). The tabs at the top stand for the different card families: equipment cards (inventory and sets), special cards and quick-travel cards. To find the cards you want, use the filter checkboxes on the right. Some windows also have a drop-down menu at the top.
npc.124: This is the team management window. All your teams are listed here. They're sorted by strength, from strongest to weakest, and your strongest team sets your coach's level (if your best team has a strength equal to level 14, your coach is level 14 too). To change a team, drag a fighter from your reserve (bottom right) onto the team to add them, and drag them back out to remove them. To recruit a new fighter, click the "Recruit" button at the bottom right of the window. They'll appear in your reserve, and from there you can send them to a team. Don't forget that the most important rule when building a team is to never exceed 6,000 budget points.
npc.125: Bug report screen.\n\nTell us what went wrong and, if you can, how to trigger it again, filling in each field. Hit Confirm and the team behind the game gets it instantly. They won't write back personally, but they'll chase the fix as fast as they can!
npc.126: Game options menu.\n\nTweak the settings to taste here. Watch out with the video ones: they can make the game crawl, or stop it from running altogether!
npc.127: This is your letterbox window. Thanks to the letterbox, you can send and receive messages to and from other coaches, whether they're online or not. It works like email, and you can even send coach cards by dragging them into the slots provided when you write a new message.
npc.128: You are on the new message window. This window lets you send a message to a coach (online or not). To do that, type their name and click the Validate button next to it, which checks that the recipient exists. Then just give your message a title, write it, and click Send. You can also attach coach cards. There are "Attachments" slots where you simply place the card(s) you want the other coach to receive.
npc.129: You're on the Card Master window! The Card Master is a minor demon who swaps your cards for cards he owns. To do this, select the card you're interested in from the left window. You can select several at once with the SHIFT key. Once you've picked your card(s), the price in pesetas the Card Master asks for them appears underneath. Now drag cards from your inventory into the Card Master's exchange area (at the bottom of the left window) until you reach or exceed the required value. The total value of the cards you're giving up appears just above it, to the left of the "/" symbol. When you have enough cards, click the "Buy" button. A window will confirm the deal, and your new cards will be in your inventory.
npc.130: You are in the quick-travel window. Quick travel takes you between the points of the Great Clock. To use it you need the card for its destination. Quick-travel cards are mostly won when your coach levels up.
npc.131: The chat window is at the bottom right of your screen. Use it to talk to other players. The chat has several channels so you can choose who you talk to. To switch channel, use its shortcut. The main channels are: The "General" channel, to talk to players nearby (shortcut: '/s'). The "Clan" channel, to talk to your clan (shortcut: '/c'). The "Trade" channel, to swap cards. Everyone in your area can see it, but you can only post once every 30 seconds ('/t'). The "Private" channel, to talk to one person only ('/w' followed by a space and the coach's name). The tabs above the chat let you choose which channels to show and switch between setups quickly.
npc.132: Fighter info panel.\n\nEverything worth knowing about a fighter, whether it's yours or your rival's, lives in this panel.
npc.133: Not available yet. Who knows, maybe later!
npc.134: You are in the end-of-fight window.\n\nThis window sums up the key info: who won, how long the match lasted and which cards the winner took (to win cards, you need to win at least two matches in a row). You'll also see info on both coaches, such as their level.
npc.135: Fight kickoff screen.\n\nA quick peek at the enemy squad and a few stats on whoever you're about to face, be it one coach or a crowd.
npc.136: You are in the placement phase. During this phase you can position your characters on the available start cells of the board. To move a character, click on it (it will light up) and then click the cell where you want it. If the cell is already occupied, the two characters swap places.
npc.137: You are in the card trading window, where you can give and receive cards safely. It's simple: first drag the cards you want to give (or swap) into the slots next to your coach's name. Now wait for the other coach to place theirs. Once you've checked them and know what you want, tick "Ready". If you've ticked "Ready" and the other coach changes the cards they're offering, your "Ready" box clears automatically. That's normal: it's a safety measure so nobody can pull their cards at the last second and cheat you. So relax, trades in this window are safe!
npc.138: Fighter creation screen.\n\nStill lost after the opening tutorial? Flip through the player's manual in the game's install folder.
npc.139: This is the fighter editing window.\n\nIf you still don't understand how to edit a fighter after the opening tutorial, check the player's manual in the Pippop Arena installation folder.
npc.140: Team builder. Put your new squad together here. Remember, no fighters means no matches, so add some! The one rule that really counts when building a team: keep the budget under 6,000 points.
npc.141: Co-op team builder. Build a squad together with someone you've added as a friend. Same golden rule as always: the budget tops out at 6,000 points.
npc.142: Scouting phase.\n\nStudy your opponent's fighters here: their squad, their spells, and where they're standing.
npc.143: You are in a challenge. Challenges are fights that don't count towards any ranking, but they can help you learn the game or sharpen your skills. Some are designed for experienced players, so don't worry if you don't beat them first time. Whatever happens, you won't lose anything by failing a challenge. Some of them will reward you with coach cards, though!
npc.146: Oi, pal!\n\nWhat's a newbie like you doing around here? The Rabid Roosters ring a bell? Shall I have your coffin built now, or sometime later?
npc.147: We've just rolled into the Great Clock, and honestly? It's no welcome party.
npc.148: Keep your eyes peeled, since some Minute Demons wander about. Trust me, obey them without fuss; they hate being talked back to.
npc.149: Alright, I'm slipping away now, this place wears me out.
npc.150: One more thing: which mouse key do you walk with, the right one or the left? (Changed your mind later? Just flip it in Options.)
npc.151: Cross the bridge on your left, then stick to the trail. I'm off now, this place reeks of sulfur...
npc.152: Hey, adventurer! I can't believe how small you are! Did you forget to grow up or something? Anyway, unless you've been living under a rock for centuries, you'll know who I am. Just in case: I'm Demon III, and I'm looking for coaches, real tough ones! Prove to me you're not a total pushover...
npc.153:
Want out of here? Beat the three trials I'm about to hand you. Or you can stay put and grow moss in this corner, your call...
But first, recruit three fighters. Zero fighters, zero trials. Clear enough for that thick skull?
npc.154: Hmm, your squad's overflowing. Click one of your fighters to select them, then hit the X to show them the door. Swing back by if you still want more recruits.
npc.155: Why's my hairdo getting that look? I'm a Swordsman, a bold and spotless fighter. Our motto: swing first, think later! Or was it the other way round? Can't recall...
npc.156: Greetings, traveler! Word is you're fresh meat around here... I'm an Archer, and nobody out-shoots me. Shall I demo it? Turn tail and run!
npc.157: Look, a newcomer... what a lovely surprise! What have you brought me? Nothing?! I'm a Gold-digger, and pesetas are my passion. You don't mind if I take a peek in your purse?
npc.158: Lost, are we? Relax, you're in good hands. I'm a Bulwark, a top-tier guardian. Our motto: never leave the house uncovered!
npc.159: Odd, I don't remember calling for you... You're new? I'm a Tamer: I summon, tame and train creatures. Brilliant in a fight, and handy when I'm craving some fur-lined boots...
npc.160: Evening, adventurer! I'm a Shade: thief and assassin. Sure, it's no bragging matter... but I promise I'm handy! And the day a shiny gem catches your eye, my face will pop into your head...
npc.161: Hey you! Welcome aboard! I'm a Fury, a.k.a. a Berserker. Every hit I take just makes me stronger! Feel like landing a few on me? I'm running a bit low today...
npc.162: Yo, rookie! I'm a Gambler, a hardcore player. High rollers don't scare me! When the bug bites, nothing stops me... Fancy a quick game? Friendly, obviously...
npc.163: Welcome, adventurer! I don't recognise your face, so you must be new here. I'm a Healer, and my speciality is healing with words. The big booboos are my department. In short, I'm the great remedy! As they say...
npc.164: Hey there, kiddo! Gardener by trade. Between salves and poisons, I've got time to play with dolls! Laugh away, but if you ever cross paths with them, I doubt you'll still be chuckling...
npc.165: I bid you welcome, adventurer. I'm a Clockmaker, and I control time. Slow down an enemy? Teleport? Easy! And yes, my friend... knowing how to fight is as important as knowing when to fight.
npc.166: Hey there! Hic!... frien hic!... I'm a Panda brawler, and my power comes straight from the hic! bottle... Whoa, the room's spinning! But if you're curious hic! about me, buy me a few rounds and we'll chat, hic!
npc.167:
Next up: the class masters, who'll set you straight. Hunt them down under Services → Learning.
Feeling idle? Open Team, then Story, and hit Create fighter to recruit without the walk.
npc.168: Nice! Your squad seems to know its stuff. Now you can take on my 3 trials. Ready?
npc.169: Pulling my leg? Where are the fighters I asked for? Dropped them on the road? One more shot for you, so keep your eyes on the prize this time. We didn't come here to goof off!
npc.182: Your interface, as you can tell, is still bare-bones.
npc.183: Right, you look a bit slow, so I'll explain: the little rectangle at the bottom right is the Chat. You can use it to talk to other coaches like you. It has other uses too, but you'll find those later... if you survive.
npc.184: This panel is where you organize your squad. Give it a tap.
npc.185: Honestly, your squad's emptier than a Swordsman's skull!
npc.186: Next stop: the Class Masters. They're the ones who sign off on your first three fighters!
npc.187: To find them, we need to head north-west. If you get lost, check the route indicator here.
npc.188: What are you doing standing there? Move it! You should've been gone ages ago! Need help? Just tap me.
npc.189: Hang on, achievements? What's that supposed to be?
npc.190: Grrr! Fine. This little icon tracks the achievements you unlock. You'll be seeing it pop up a lot while you find your feet in the Great Clock.
npc.191: Move along! Your squad is out there up north, waiting on you.
npc.192: Time I filled you in on our whereabouts. Quite the mess, huh?
npc.193: Those are the Demons of the Hours, our masters, who built the Great Clock. They pulled bits of land from here and there, in different eras, from other worlds in this universe. That's why the place looks like a giant construction site!
npc.194: Hold on, you haven't recruited a single fighter yet! Up and at 'em, lazybones, no time to loaf about!
npc.195: Wait, Demon III is here?! Consider yourself lucky. Tap him to get a word in.
npc.196: Think of Demon III as the gatekeeper. Get past him and the Time Wardens take over, with the major tournaments right after.
npc.197: Care for a game? I dare you to clear my 3 trials!
npc.198: Finally! The Class Masters are right in front of us!
npc.199: Each one will walk you through what makes their class tick.
npc.200: Well done! You're not doing badly for a beginner. A little tip that might help: when you hit an enemy from the side, you deal 20% extra damage. Hit them in the back and you deal 40% extra. Always good to know, right?
npc.201: Clear this new trial and I'll break down what experience is.
npc.202: Wow, serious potential there! Looks can be deceiving, ha ha!
npc.101: Nice manners, I approve. Tap the glowing spot now. Quick, my schedule's packed!
npc.102: This is a ready-made squad. Soon you'll be able to try it out, or kick off a battle by hitting...
npc.104: Those swords again, eh? Good. I can see your finger twitching, but keep it still for now.
npc.115: Oi! Hands off! Put that down and listen up for a sec, you'll need it!
npc.203: Every fight you take makes your team tougher and a little more experienced.
npc.204: Shut the fight summary and head to your team panel. That's where you'll learn how to spend those XP.
npc.205: Nice one! Next, hit the “Path” button right over here.
npc.206: There you go! Your Path tracks how each fighter grows. Yours hasn't moved off the starting line yet.
npc.207: Most spheres on your Path hand out a bonus, but they only count once you've landed on them.
npc.208: Hover over any sphere to see its bonus. Start with the first one. Clicking picks it, but since you're still finding your feet, I'll make the pick for you.
npc.209: Look bottom right: a “Buy” button has just popped up, right under the sphere's XP cost.
npc.210: You've got 3 XP and the first sphere only costs 2, so you're covered. Smash that “Buy” button.
npc.211: Done, it's yours! Your fighter is now carrying that bonus. Stack up enough XP and the next sphere is yours to grab. The deeper you wander down the Path, the juicier the rewards.
npc.212: Heads up: the last challenge from Demon III is coming up. Remember, every fighter walks their own Path, so spread your experience around and let each one climb their spheres.
npc.213: Excellent! That Mangler finally got what was coming. Look at it now, scattered like crumbs!
npc.214: Did you see that? Demon III has recognised your strength and given you access to new interface options. You can recruit up to 4 fighters without going to see the class masters, just by clicking on the team panel.
npc.215: Plenty of time to poke around those options later. For now, just keep this in mind: your achievements and your grimoire are always one click away.
npc.216: Ah, the grimoire, my favourite! Every card you win, buy or trade ends up in there.
npc.217: Cards can also dress up your fighters, and they look fabulous doing it. The coaches who go all out wear legendary outfits, and those outfits come with bonuses too. Style counts, ha ha!
npc.218: We'll get into that another time. Onward!
npc.219: Here we are! Now click on the notice board in the lobby.
npc.220: As you can see, clicking the notice board opened your grimoire. To go and see demon I, find the “Demon I Lair” card and double-click it. Go on, don't be shy! Click!
npc.221: This place is looking lovely, isn't it?
npc.222: Talk about luck! We landed just in time and in exactly the right spot. Demon I is somewhere nearby. He's the one signing people up for the great tournament.
npc.223: Don't hang back, champion! Dash over and get yourself registered.
npc.224: Meet Imix. Watch out, he's a seasoned summoner and his hits sting. To walk out of this fight in one piece, make use of the arena's bonus cells.
npc.225: Begin a turn standing on a bonus cell and a fighter cashes in whatever it's offering: AP, resistance, or some other perk.
npc.226: Park yourself on the resistance bonus cells at the right moment and victory is within reach!
npc.227: There he is! That sly Ik'. He's no heavyweight, but his arena is booby-trapped. Eyes open!
npc.228: Penalty squares wake up as each turn begins. Step on a lethal square and you're gone in a heartbeat; a trap square just leaves you hurt.
npc.229: Ik' loves his pull spells, dragging fighters right into his traps. Mind yourself!
npc.230: Final tip: a stabilisation spell is your anchor, keeping you planted so you don't get tugged onto a penalty square. Note it!
npc.231: This is Ak'bal, otherwise known as “the sniper”. To beat him, creep closer while sheltering behind the obstacles, and keep your event cards in sight.
npc.232: Your event cards sit in the top right corner. The one on top governs the current turn and hands out perks or drawbacks to every fighter on the field.
npc.233: The other two come into play next turn. A sharp coach always checks them before choosing a move.
npc.234: For this one, pick the event cards that suit you. When Ak'bal's cards show up, get under cover!
npc.235: Meet K'an. He looks scrawny, but he's quick and packs a punch.
npc.236: Your action cards are your ticket to beating him. Each one is a special spell good for a single use per battle, and any fighter on your roster can fire it.
npc.237: Honest truth: in the fight coming up, it's all decided on turn one. Winning hinges on chaining your action cards well.
npc.238: Right, now it gets real. Put everything I've taught you to work!
npc.239: One final pointer: lock onto the first target you plan to hit. 3... 2... 1... Good luck!
npc.241: You're all set to take on rival coaches. One small step first: lock in your sign-up with Demon I.
npc.242: Alright, that's enough fun. You need an opponent to start building a name for yourself. Open your team panel and find one.
npc.243: Feel like a bout in the great tournament? Pop over to the Tournaments card in the lobby. Open all hours, as far as I know!
npc.244: The great tournament is where fame is earned. Rack up wins and you might end up the crowd's favourite coach.
npc.245: To check out the season's top coaches, press the “Ranking” button.
npc.246: Want your name on the board? Land somewhere in the top 2000 coaches. Hit the “Coach” button to find out your precise spot.
npc.247: Remember, your fighters aren't invincible. They need plenty of TLC.
npc.248: Now and then, send them to the bench for a breather, since tiredness and injuries can catch up with them.
npc.249: Their morale matters too. Don't let them pile up defeats or get knocked out too often, and don't forget the bench is part of the team!
npc.250: That's a chat for another day. Once you're feeling confident, you're free to kick off a bout in the great tournament.
npc.251: So you fancy your chances at the great tournament? Perfect timing, we've lost a few coaches recently. Fresh blood is always welcome!
npc.252: Your registration only sticks once you clear the qualifying trials. The crowd has zero patience for rookies wasting their time.
npc.253: Beat the five Lords of Time (Story, chapter 2) and the great tournament will swing its doors wide open for you.
npc.254: Word on the street says all five Lords of Time are already history. Nice one! Hit me with a high five... oh, you've already taken it! Ha ha!
npc.255: Alright, alright. You've earned your place at the great tournament, so here's your pass. Tournaments in the Calendar are open to you now.
npc.256: Splendid! You made it through alive. Didn't look that tough, did you? Relax, I'm only teasing!
npc.257: You're looking a bit jittery... a touch queasy, maybe? Relax, plenty have walked this path before, and a few even walked out again...
npc.258: Well, if you want your freedom back, you'll need to prove you've got backbone and nerve.
npc.259: Feels like we're in for some serious fun! I'll walk you through your opening moves in the arena, and I'm dying to see what you can pull off!
npc.267: Oh, so you reckon you can flatten me? Demon I must be desperate, sending a squirt like you... Go on then, impress me!
npc.268: You, beat me? Adorable. Demon I must be scraping the bottom of the barrel if this is who he sends... Go on, let's see what you've got!
npc.269: Think you'll floor me? Poor Demon I, his bench must be empty if he's sending someone like you. Come on, prove your worth!
npc.270: So you want to beat me... Looks like Demon I is short on troops if he's sending you. Right then, let's see what you're capable of.
npc.271: Ha ha ha! And you think beating every other demon here means you can hold a candle to me? Bring it on!
npc.273:
Look at you go, kiddo! Seems you're ready for nastier rivals, and the Lords of Time are itching to meet you (Story, chapter 2).
See you soon! Swing by whenever, I've got fresh challenges stashed away.
npc.274: You're not on my level yet. Topple the other four Lords of Time, then come back and maybe I'll accept a duel.
npc.275: Mwa ha ha! I've snatched Anselmo and I'm keeping him forever! Unless you shatter my crystal buddies...
npc.277: Spot the 37? That's II, one of Chikchan's servants. You'll remember him: he's the one who squared up to you the day you landed in the Great Clock.
npc.278: He's set up a jail to hold a prisoner his boss cares deeply about, and he swears it can't be breached. Why not show him otherwise?
npc.279: Careful! A 100% resistance doesn't make him untouchable. Crank your damage bonuses high enough and your blows will still connect.
npc.280: Did I just hear that right? Planning a jailbreak? Ha! Not a chance. I upgraded my boss's glass cage. Nobody's getting in now!
npc.282: Right, let's get serious. First up: place your Swordsman while the positioning phase is running.
npc.283: There's no clock during training, but in a real fight you'll only get 30 seconds to position your whole squad.
npc.284: To place a fighter, select them with a left click, then select the cell you want to move them to. If another fighter is there, they'll swap places (no worries here, since your Swordsman is on his own).
npc.285: Once you've got the knack, hit “Ready”.
npc.286: Once the placing wraps up, you'll have spotted the 10-second observation window that follows.
npc.287: During observation, you can track down the enemies and check their stats by clicking the turn order bar in the top left.
npc.288: For training, I've switched off the 30-second timer that limits each turn in a real fight, so you've got all the time you need to check the turn order bar.
npc.289: When you're good to go, head for the Woolly. Three MP (Movement Points) are yours to spend closing in: click the square just ahead of it.
npc.290: Don't sweat it! Close the gap by clicking the square directly ahead of it. Which button does the trick (left or right) is whatever you picked on arrival, and swapping is always an option.
npc.291: Nice work! Time to finish it with Pressure. Pick the spell from the bar in the lower left, then tap your target.
npc.292: Hmm, not bad, but next time target the Woolly's cell, or it'll be a struggle to bring it down...
npc.293: Splendid, it's connected! One more Pressure and it's finished, and that closes out our drill.
npc.294: Your AP (Action Points) total sits in a blue bubble, bottom left. Pressure costs 3, so recast it if the pool allows; when it doesn't, pass the turn and you'll regain 6.
npc.300: Oof! One of your fighters took a hit. Bad news: leave the injury untreated and they'll struggle to fight properly from here on.
npc.301: The truth is, plenty of injuries end in death. Still, they're your fighters, so the call is yours.
npc.302: Sure, leaving them untreated is your call... Just keep in mind that a fighter who's worn out or battered is far more likely to take fresh damage.
npc.303: Hmm, I believe I overheard a coach the other day raving about a pile of healing goodies from a card pack...
npc.304: Once a resurrection potion is in your hands, make for the graveyard and collect your fallen fighter. Lost? The lobby will point you in the right direction.
npc.305: For now, my tip is to send the fallen fighter to the graveyard, where they can at least catch some rest.
npc.306: Relax, it's not the end of the world. Recall those card packs I mentioned? Besides healing goodies, they can hide resurrection potions too.
npc.307: Told you so! Sorry to rub it in, but you ignored me and now a fighter has fallen!
npc.308: Oi, you! Yes, you. Quit gawking and come over here. What, you can't get around? Easy: right click or left click, your call.
